fanoutqa_012180.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone :: Characters :: part 02 :: chunk_0003
fanoutqa_012180.x:
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone :: Characters :: part 02 :: chunk_0003
* [Draco Malfoy](/wiki/Draco_Malfoy "Draco Malfoy") is a slim, pale boy who speaks in a bored drawl. He is arrogant about his skill in Quidditch, and despises anyone who is not a pure-blood wizard and wizards who do not share his views. His parents had supported Voldemort, but changed sides after the dark wizard's disappearance, claiming they had been [bewitched](/wiki/Imperius_Curse "Imperius Curse"). Draco avoids direct confrontations and tries to get Harry and his friends into trouble.
* [Oliver Wood](/wiki/Oliver_Wood_(Harry_Potter) "Oliver Wood (Harry Potter)") is a fifth year who acts as Harry's Quidditch captain and keeper for the Gryffindor Quidditch team.
* [Professor Quirrell](/wiki/Professor_Quirrell "Professor Quirrell") is a twitching, stammering, and nervous man who teaches Defence Against the Dark Arts. Reputedly he was a brilliant scholar, but his nerve was shattered by an encounter with vampires. Quirrell wears a turban to conceal the fact that he is voluntarily possessed by Voldemort, whose face appears on the back of Quirrell's head.
* Professor [Severus Snape](/wiki/Severus_Snape "Severus Snape"), who has a hooked nose, sallow complexion, and greasy black hair, teaches Potions, but would prefer to teach Defence Against the Dark Arts. Snape favours pupils in his own House of Slytherin, and appears to delight in humiliating those from other houses, especially Harry. Several incidents, beginning with the shooting pain in Harry's scar during the start-of-term feast, lead Harry and his friends to think Snape is aiding Voldemort.
* [Argus Filch](/wiki/Argus_Filch "Argus Filch"), the school caretaker who knows the school's [secret passages](/wiki/Hogwarts#Passages "Hogwarts") better than anyone else except, perhaps, the Weasley twins. His cat, Mrs. Norris, aids his constant hunt for misbehaving pupils.

Lynch credits her chosen career path in healthcare to her family life experiences.[[5]](#cite_note-intro-5) In 2004, Lynch was appointed president of Cigna Dental.[[6]](#cite_note-6) The following year, she took on a position that combined leadership of Cigna Group Insurance and Cigna Dental.[[7]](#cite_note-7) She left Cigna in 2009 to become president of Magellan Health Services.[[8]](#cite_note-CEO-8)

In 2012, Lynch left Magellan and joined Aetna as executive vice president and head of specialty products.[[9]](#cite_note-9) Three months after joining Aetna, Lynch led the integration of [Coventry Health Care](/wiki/Coventry_Health_Care "Coventry Health Care"), which was the largest health care acquisition at the time.[[10]](#cite_note-leadersmag-10) In 2015, Lynch became Aetna's first female president, a role she retained through the $70 billion acquisition of Aetna by CVS Health in 2018.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

On February 1, 2021, Lynch became president and CEO of CVS Health following the retirement of [Larry Merlo](/wiki/Larry_Merlo "Larry Merlo").[[12]](#cite_note-Valinsky-12) The appointment made her the highest-ranking female CEO on the Fortune 500 list and the 40th female chief executive on the Fortune 500 list.[[12]](#cite_note-Valinsky-12)[[13]](#cite_note-:50-13) Under Lynch's leadership, CVS Health administered the COVID-19 vaccine in more than 40,000 long-term care facilities and in CVS Pharmacy locations in 50 states, Puerto Rico and Washington, D.C.[[14]](#cite_note-14) She was also credited with overhauling their drug pricing business model to decrease costs borne by consumers. Under Lynch, CVS announced CVS CostVantage, a [cost-plus](/wiki/Cost-plus_contract "Cost-plus contract") model that based the cost of prescription drugs on the amount paid by CVS plus a small markup.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

In 2023, Lynch's total compensation from CVS Health was $21.6 million, representing a CEO-to-median worker [pay ratio]

fanoutqa_024724.t: Gone with the Wind (film) :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
fanoutqa_024724.x:
Gone with the Wind (film) :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
*Gone With the Wind* received generally positive reviews upon its release on December 15, 1939. While the casting was widely praised, the long running time received criticism. At the [12th Academy Awards](/wiki/12th_Academy_Awards "12th Academy Awards"), *Gone with the Wind* received ten [Academy Awards](/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (eight competitive, two honorary) from thirteen nominations, including wins for [Best Picture](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), [Best Director](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Director "Academy Award for Best Director") (Fleming), [Best Adapted Screenplay](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") (posthumously awarded to Sidney Howard), [Best Actress](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") (Leigh), and [Best Supporting Actress](/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") ([Hattie McDaniel](/wiki/Hattie_McDaniel "Hattie McDaniel"), becoming the first [African American](/wiki/African_American "African American") to win an Academy Award). It set records for the total number of wins and nominations at the time.

*Gone with the Wind* was immensely popular when first released. It became the [highest-earning film made up to that point](/wiki/Timeline_of_highest-grossing_films "Timeline of highest-grossing films") and held the record for over a quarter of a century. When [adjusted for monetary inflation](/wiki/Real_versus_nominal_value_(economics) "Real versus nominal value (economics)"), it is still [the highest-grossing film in history](/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_films_adjusted_for_inflation "List of highest-grossing films adjusted for inflation"). [![A bald eagle](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Bald_eagle_about_to_fly_in_Alaska_%282016%29.jpg/250px-Bald_eagle_about_to_fly_in_Alaska_%282016%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Bald_eagle_about_to_fly_in_Alaska_(2016).jpg)

The [bald eagle](/wiki/Bald_eagle "Bald eagle"), the [national emblem of the United States](/wiki/Bald_eagle#National_symbol_of_the_United_States "Bald eagle") since 1782 and officially declared the national bird in 2024[[216]](#cite_note-233)

The U.S. is one of 17 [megadiverse countries](/wiki/Megadiverse_countries "Megadiverse countries") containing large numbers of [endemic species](/wiki/List_of_endangered_animals_of_North_America "List of endangered animals of North America"): about 17,000 species of [vascular plants](/wiki/Vascular_plant "Vascular plant") occur in the contiguous United States and Alaska, and over 1,800 species of [flowering plants](/wiki/Flowering_plant "Flowering plant") are found in Hawaii, few of which occur on the mainland.[[217]](#cite_note-234) The United States is home to 428 [mammal](/wiki/Mammal "Mammal") species, 784 birds, 311 reptiles, 295 [amphibians](/wiki/Amphibian "Amphibian"),[[218]](#cite_note-Current_Results_#_of_native_species_in_the_US-235) and around 91,000 insect species.[[219]](#cite_note-236)
